requirements.title: Identity and responsible owner
requirements.normative_text: The provider MUST include a system identifier and the name of the person or organization responsible for the described system in the description record for each system version covered by the declaration.
requirements.applicability: Provider-authored description records for the specific system version and operating scope named in a provider declaration; this candidate does not impose a runtime effectiveness result.
requirements.rationale: Bind a declaration to a described subject and responsible party.
requirements.implementation_notes: Proposed document obligation derived from existing OAS concepts. Review the stated open questions before adoption; do not infer complete or effective implementation from a description.
requirements.verification_notes: Inspect the record for a nonempty system identifier and named responsible party; this does not verify legal ownership.

sources.exact_excerpt: Establishes clear identity, provenance and ownership for agents, ensuring accountability throughout their lifecycle.

open_questions.title: Actor and applicability
open_questions.detail: Approve whether this first set governs provider description records only, or must also specify runtime behavior. All candidates explicitly target description records; no runtime efficacy follows.

open_questions.title: Risk applicability
open_questions.detail: Define R0–R4 assignment criteria, decision authority, reassessment and conflict rules before risk-conditioned obligations.

open_questions.title: Ownership
open_questions.detail: Clarify accountable owner versus legal ownership, multiple owners, and acceptable organization identifiers.

open_questions.title: Provenance
open_questions.detail: Approve minimum provenance granularity and treatment of composite, externally hosted or continuously updated systems.

open_questions.title: Permissions and capability completeness
open_questions.detail: Approve scope boundaries, dynamically discovered tools, permission exceptions and whether runtime denial behavior belongs in release 1.

open_questions.title: Prohibited actions and guardrails
open_questions.detail: Identify who defines prohibited actions and context-specific policies; decide whether effectiveness criteria are required. No universal legal or safety prohibition list is invented.

open_questions.title: Human control
open_questions.detail: Review override feasibility, escalation thresholds, response latency and failure behavior. No unsupported latency or always-on human mandate is authored.

open_questions.title: Evidence and verification
open_questions.detail: Review minimum test methods, evidence accessibility, privacy, retention and whether evidence plans alone suffice. No completeness or conformance follows from evidence presence.

open_questions.title: Lifecycle
open_questions.detail: Approve lifecycle vocabulary, version identity, retirement responsibilities and record retention; Registry lifecycle remains separate.

open_questions.title: Governance approval authority
open_questions.detail: OAS must identify its authorized adopter, decision procedure/quorum and approval record. None is established by repository code.

open_questions.title: Legacy domain mapping
open_questions.detail: Review every ambiguous reporting label and approve migration disposition before canonical report adoption.

open_questions.title: Release scope adequacy
open_questions.detail: Decide whether these traceable description obligations constitute a useful complete first standard; no claim of complete autonomous-system governance is made.
